title: Finite unions and closed subsets of relatively proper supports on spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to Y$ be locally of finite type on etale scheme charts. Use the point spaces with their atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A closed subspace is a representable closed immersion, tested on schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Proper means separated (closed relative diagonal), quasi-compact, locally of finite type and universally closed, meaning closed on point spaces after every algebraic-space base change. For a closed subset $T\subseteq|X|$, its reduced induced closed subspace is the closed subspace with point set $T$ and reduced etale scheme charts. Say that $T$ is proper over $Y$ when this reduced induced subspace is proper over $Y$. Then this is equivalent both to the existence of some closed subspace with point set $T$ proper over $Y$, and to every closed subspace with that point set being proper over $Y$. If $T$ is proper over $Y$ and $T^{\prime}\subseteq T$ is closed in $|X|$, then $T^{\prime}$ is proper over $Y$. For every finite family of closed subsets $T_1,\ldots,T_n$ proper over $Y$, including the empty family, $\bigcup_{j=1}^n T_j$ is proper over $Y$.

source.place: Tags 0CZC (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), 0CZE (lemma-closed-closed-proper-over-base), 0CZH (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base); reduced induced subspaces: spaces-properties.tex Tag 047X (definition-reduced-induced-space).

proof.text: Every closed subspace $W\hookrightarrow X$ is locally of finite type over $Y$: its inclusion is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], hence locally of finite type, and composition with $f$ preserves local finite type by [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], specialized to algebraic spaces. Also, [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] supplies every reduced induced closed subspace used below, including its closed embedding and its point-space identification. No Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 0CZC (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), local finite type requirement; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 04XZ and 03XG; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IQ

proof.text: Fix $T$ and any closed structure $Z\hookrightarrow X$ on $T$. Let $R_Z\hookrightarrow Z$ be the reduced induced subspace on all of $|Z|$, by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Its composite into $X$ is a closed immersion by [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus], specialized to spaces. It has reduced charts and point image $T$, so uniqueness in [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] identifies it, over $X$, with the reduced induced structure $R_T\hookrightarrow X$. Thus $R_T\hookrightarrow Z$ is a thickening: a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism on point spaces. Apply [lem-sfb-space-thickening-topological-properties] with source thickening $R_T\hookrightarrow Z$ and target thickening $\mathrm{id}_Y$. The maps $R_T\to Y$ and $Z\to Y$ have simultaneously each of separatedness, quasi-compactness and universal closedness. Both are locally of finite type by step 1. Therefore $R_T\to Y$ is proper if and only if $Z\to Y$ is proper. Since $R_T$ itself is a closed structure on $T$, this proves all three equivalent formulations, including the existential and universal ones.

source.place: Tag 0CZC (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), reduction proof of structure independence; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZY (lemma-thicken-property-morphisms), parts (3), (4), (6)

proof.text: For $T\prime\subseteq T$ closed, let $Z=R_T$, which is proper over $Y$. The inverse image of $T\prime$ in $|Z|$ is closed. Give it its reduced induced structure $W\hookrightarrow Z$ by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. This inclusion is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], so $W\to Y$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition]. Its composite into $X$ is a closed immersion by [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus], and has point image $T\prime$. Step 2 therefore proves that $T\prime$ is proper over $Y$.

For a nonempty finite family set $T=\bigcup_iT_i$, a closed set, and let $Z=R_T$ and $Z_i=R_{T_i}$. Put $W_i=Z_i\times_XZ$. By the arbitrary-base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], both $W_i\to Z_i$ and $W_i\to Z$ are closed immersions, and the latter has point image the inverse image of $T_i$ in $|Z|$. In particular these images cover $|Z|$. Do not assert that $W_i$ is reduced. Since $Z_i\to Y$ is proper, [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper] and [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition] make $W_i\to Y$ proper.

source.place: Tag 0CZH (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base), closed component supports; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IQ and its closed-pullback support statement

proof.text: Form $D=\coprod_iW_i$ using [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct]; finitely many chosen atlases have a scheme coproduct in the fixed site, so its size hypothesis holds. The scheme-test partition and cartesian squares in [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] identify the summands with disjoint clopen subspaces and show that this decomposition persists after any base change: apply the partition to every scheme test of that base change. In particular point spaces are disjoint topological unions. The map $D\to Y$ is proper, directly from the four defining conditions. It is locally of finite type: a disjoint union of atlases of the $W_i$ gives chart maps locally equal to those of $W_i\to Y$; apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]. Its diagonal on the clopen blocks $W_i\times_YW_j$ is empty if $i\ne j$ and is $\Delta_{W_i/Y}$ if $i=j$. On scheme tests these are closed immersions, so the diagonal is a closed immersion (closedness and surjectivity of the defining ring-sheaf quotient are local on this clopen partition). Over an affine test the source is a finite disjoint union of quasi-compact point spaces, hence quasi-compact by taking the union of finitely many finite subcovers. After any base change the image of a closed set is the finite union of its closed images from the proper summands, hence closed.

source.place: Tag 0CZH (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base), finite disjoint union of proper sources; spaces.tex Tags 02WQ and 0F15, with componentwise verification of properness

proof.text: The component maps $W_i\to Z$ induce $a:D\to Z$. It is surjective because their point images cover $|Z|$. It is universally closed: after every algebraic-space base change to $Z$, the source remains the finite disjoint union of the base changes of $W_i$; those maps are closed immersions by [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus] and hence proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper]. The image of a closed subset is the finite union of the resulting closed images. Surjectivity persists under arbitrary base change by the fibre-product point-surjectivity assertion in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus].

source.place: Tag 0CZH (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base), universally closed covering of the union; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-relative-uc-surjection-separated] applied over $B=Y$ to $a:D\to Z$, the properness of $D\to Y$ implies that $Z\to Y$ is separated. For an affine scheme $A\to Y$, the continuous surjection $|D\times_YA|\to|Z\times_YA|$ has quasi-compact source, so its target is quasi-compact: pull back any open cover and push its finite subcover down using surjectivity. Thus $Z\to Y$ is quasi-compact. For an arbitrary space $Y\prime\to Y$ and closed $C\subseteq|Z\times_YY\prime|$, continuity of point maps from [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] makes $a_{Y\prime}^{-1}(C)$ closed. Surjectivity gives the equality of point images $(Z\times_YY\prime\to Y\prime)(C)=(D\times_YY\prime\to Y\prime)(a_{Y\prime}^{-1}(C))$. The right side is closed by properness of $D\to Y$. Hence $Z\to Y$ is universally closed. Together with local finite type from step 1 these conditions prove $Z\to Y$ proper, which is exactly properness of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0CZH (lemma-union-closed-proper-over-base), descent from the finite union of sources; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 05Z2(4) and 08AJ (lemma-image-proper-is-proper), with the closed-image argument written out

proof.text: For the empty family the union is empty. The empty sheaf coproduct represents the empty scheme, as its scheme-test sections are exactly those given for the empty index set in [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition]. It is a reduced closed subspace of $X$, hence is the reduced induced structure on the empty closed set by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. The map from the empty space to $Y$ is a closed immersion on every scheme test, and therefore proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper]. This proves the empty-family clause; the same arguments permit empty summands and repeated $T_i$.
